title: Unified scheduling for visual ETL flows and query books in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Visual ETL flows and query books in SageMaker Unified Studio can now be scheduled in place; behind it EventBridge Scheduler starts a SageMaker Training job that runs the flow.
Basic scheduling feature; later Unified Studio workflow posts cover orchestration more fully.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
authors: Noritaka Sekiyama, Daniel Obi, Gal Heyne, Yuhang Huang, Vasudevan Venkataramanan

title: How Flutter UKI optimizes data pipelines with AWS Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow
key_points: Flutter UKI moved from a single self-managed Airflow on EC2 to several MWAA environments, spreading thousands of generated DAGs across them and running every task as a pod on EKS.
A thin wrapper around the Kubernetes Pod Operator hides repeated settings and absorbs version changes, so thousands of DAGs do not need editing on each upgrade.
AWS reports about 5,500 DAGs and over 60,000 DAG runs a day.
services: Amazon MWAA, Apache Airflow, Amazon EKS, AWS Secrets Manager
decision: Native Airflow operators vs pod-per-task execution on Kubernetes for a large DAG estate
authors: Flutter UKI — Monica Cujerean, Ionut Hedesiu, Nidhi Agrawal, John Kellet, Sidhanth Muralidhar

title: How BMW Group built a serverless terabyte-scale data transformation architecture with dbt and Amazon Athena
key_points: BMW's cloud cost analytics team replaced Terraform-managed Athena views with dbt models on Athena (source, prepared, semantic layers), deployed by pull request and run on schedules from GitHub Actions; AWS reports about 400 models over a 15 TB lake.
Practical patterns: separate Athena workgroups for dbt runs, dbt tests, BI refresh and ad hoc queries to see and cap cost per use; a custom backfill workflow for chosen models and date ranges.
Moving heavy logic out of BI views into materialised dbt tables raised dbt cost but cut total cost, and SPICE loads only the recent columns dashboards actually use.
services: dbt, dbt-athena, Amazon Athena, Amazon Quick Sight, AWS Glue Data Catalog, GitHub Actions
decision: BI-tool views vs dbt-materialised tables on Athena for heavy dashboard logic; one workgroup vs per-purpose workgroups for cost control
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (Athena folder: workgroup split, backfill workflow)
authors: BMW Group — Philipp Karg, Cizer Pereira, Selman Ay

title: Best practices for least privilege configuration in Amazon MWAA
key_points: How to lock down an MWAA environment: tight security groups and network ACLs, VPC endpoints with restrictive policies, and minimal deployer and execution roles.
Reference checklist for regulated MWAA setups; no design trade-off for the reader's current work.
services: Amazon MWAA, Amazon VPC, AWS IAM

title: Melting the ice — How Natural Intelligence simplified a data lake migration to Apache Iceberg
key_points: Natural Intelligence found both standard Hive-to-Iceberg routes lacking: in-place conversion needs a write freeze and a big-bang switch, a full rewrite doubles storage and pipelines.

Their hybrid kept Hive and Iceberg copies in sync at partition level in both directions (forward and reverse CDC) plus automatic schema sync, so consumers and ETL jobs could move one at a time; Snowflake users were switched through table aliases.
Final cutover registered the existing Parquet files with add_files through a Hive metastore on EMR, working around Glue's lack of table rename and migrate.
services: Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon EMR, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon DynamoDB, Snowflake
decision: In-place conversion vs full rewrite vs dual-synced hybrid for a zero-downtime Hive-to-Iceberg migration
authors: Natural Intelligence — Yonatan Dolan, Haya Axelrod Stern, Zion Rubin, Michal Urbanowicz

title: Access your existing data and resources through Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Part 2: Amazon S3, Amazon RDS, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon EMR
key_points: Part 2 covers adding existing S3 buckets, RDS PostgreSQL, DynamoDB tables and EMR clusters to a SageMaker Unified Studio project with the needed roles and connections.
Console onboarding steps; no design choices discussed.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon S3, Amazon RDS, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon EMR
authors: Noritaka Sekiyama, Chanu Damarla, Daiyan Alamgir, Lakshmi Nair, Sakti Mishra, Vipin Mohan

title: Access your existing data and resources through Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Part 1: AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Redshift
key_points: Console steps to bring existing Glue catalog tables and existing Redshift clusters (via managed VPC endpoint and federated connection) into a SageMaker Unified Studio project and its business catalog.
Onboarding guide for SageMaker Unified Studio adopters.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Redshift, AWS Lake Formation
authors: Lakshmi Nair, Chanu Damarla, Daiyan Alamgir, Sakti Mishra, Noritaka Sekiyama, Vipin Mohan

title: Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse now supports attribute-based access control
key_points: Lake Formation grants can now target IAM principals by attribute (tags on the role or session) rather than naming each role.
Example gives three users different table and column access based on attributes, then checks it from Athena, Redshift and EMR.
Reduces grant sprawl when many roles share a business attribute such as department or region.
services: AWS Lake Formation, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, AWS IAM, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon EMR
decision: Named-role grants vs tag-based (LF-TBAC) vs attribute-based grants on principals for lakehouse access

title: Accelerate data pipeline creation with the new visual interface in Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion
key_points: OpenSearch Ingestion pipelines can now be built in a guided console flow that discovers sources and sinks, creates the IAM role and validates as it goes.
Console usability launch for OpenSearch users.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, Amazon OpenSearch Service

title: Read and write Apache Iceberg tables using AWS Lake Formation hybrid access mode
key_points: Hybrid access mode lets an S3 location serve two permission models at once: new readers get Lake Formation grants while existing writer pipelines keep their IAM and bucket policies.
Example: an analyst role reads an Iceberg table in Athena under Lake Formation while an EMR job upserts and changes the schema with IAM only.
A gradual path to Lake Formation that avoids rewiring every existing pipeline on day one.
services: AWS Lake Formation, Apache Iceberg, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue Data Catalog
decision: IAM-only vs full Lake Formation vs hybrid access mode when adding fine-grained readers to tables existing pipelines write

title: Accelerate your analytics with Amazon S3 Tables and Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse
key_points: Announces S3 Tables appearing in SageMaker Lakehouse next to Redshift tables published to the Glue catalog, so Athena, Redshift and Glue Spark can query and join both.
Console walkthrough with three personas; the integration is now standard and later S3 Tables posts go deeper.
services: Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue, AWS Lake Formation
authors: Sandeep Adwankar, Aditya Kalyanakrishnan, Srividya Parthasarathy

title: Integrate ThoughtSpot with Amazon Redshift using AWS IAM Identity Center
key_points: ThoughtSpot users can sign in to Redshift through IAM Identity Center with a trusted token issuer, using Okta or Entra ID, so the user's identity reaches Redshift and Lake Formation.
Setup walkthrough for one BI tool; the general Identity Center pattern is covered in other posts.
services: Amazon Redshift, AWS IAM Identity Center, ThoughtSpot
authors: ThoughtSpot — Maneesh Sharma, Ali Alladin, BP Yau, Debu Panda

title: Build unified pipelines spanning multiple AWS accounts and Regions with Amazon MWAA
key_points: One MWAA environment in a central account drives a Glue job in a second account's Region 1 and a SageMaker step in its Region 2, with S3 cross-Region replication moving the output between them.
Relies on assumed cross-account roles and custom operators; deployed with CloudFormation stack sets.
Ends with cross-account practices: narrow trust policies, per-team roles, and monitoring replication lag.
services: Amazon MWAA, AWS Glue, Amazon S3, Amazon SageMaker, AWS CloudFormation
decision: One central orchestrator assuming roles across accounts vs an orchestrator per account with event hand-offs
authors: Anubhav Gupta, Anusha Pininti, Geetha Penmatsa, Sriharsh Adari, Suba Palanisamy

title: Streamline data discovery with precise technical identifier search in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: SageMaker Catalog search now returns exact matches on technical names (columns, tables, schemas) when the term is put in double quotes.
Small search usability change, no architecture content.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog
authors: Ramesh H Singh, Jie Lan, Pradeep Misra, Rajat Mathur

title: Process millions of observability events with Apache Flink and write directly to Prometheus
key_points: Introduces an open-source Flink sink for Prometheus and Managed Prometheus, so a Flink job can push metrics straight into a time-series store.
The core idea is shifting work left: aggregate and enrich raw device events (connected-car example) in Flink so the metric store gets fewer, lower-cardinality series.
Lists what the connector leaves to the user, notably keeping samples in order per series.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, Amazon Managed Grafana
decision: Send raw events to the metrics store vs pre-aggregate in a stream processor to control series cardinality

title: Manage concurrent write conflicts in Apache Iceberg on the AWS Glue Data Catalog
key_points: Separates two kinds of Iceberg write failure: catalog commit clashes, which Iceberg retries by itself and can be tuned with table properties, and data conflicts (overlapping UPDATE, MERGE or compaction), which fail and need the job's own retry logic.
Gives a PySpark streaming MERGE that catches the validation error and retries with backoff and jitter, plus baseline retry settings for streaming writers and for compaction jobs.
Best defence is scoping: keep compaction and upserts on different partitions, or filter writes so they touch fewer files; snapshot isolation does not help the streaming-vs-compaction case.
services: Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Glue, Apache Spark
decision: Rely on built-in commit retries vs custom retry on data conflicts vs partition-scoped writes for Iceberg tables shared by streaming upserts and compaction
attaches_to: aws-bytes: File Layout Optimization (active: compaction vs concurrent writers)

title: Enhance Agentforce data security with Private Connect for Salesforce Data Cloud and Amazon Redshift – Part 3
key_points: Part 3 of the Salesforce Data Cloud zero-copy series: a self-managed PrivateLink endpoint service (Network Load Balancer in front of Redshift) so Salesforce reaches Redshift without a public endpoint.
Mostly networking steps, including how to keep the load balancer target pointed at the right IP after a Multi-AZ or Serverless failover.
Only matters to teams already running the Salesforce zero-copy integration.
services: Amazon Redshift, AWS PrivateLink, Elastic Load Balancing, Salesforce Data Cloud
authors: Salesforce — Yogesh Dhimate, Avijit Goswami, Ifetayo Stewart, Mike Patterson, Drew Loika

title: Optimize multimodal search using the TwelveLabs Embed API and Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: Partner walkthrough: TwelveLabs turns video into embeddings that combine picture, sound and speech, stored in an OpenSearch vector index.
Shows searching the videos by text, audio clip or image; a video-search use case far from the reader's pipelines.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, TwelveLabs Embed API
authors: TwelveLabs — James Le, Gitika Vijh, Kruthi Jayasimha Rao

title: Correlate telemetry data with Amazon OpenSearch Service and Amazon Managed Grafana
key_points: An OpenTelemetry collector sends logs and traces to OpenSearch through OpenSearch Ingestion and metrics to Managed Prometheus, and Grafana links the three so an engineer can jump from a metric spike to the related trace and log lines.
Application observability for microservices on EKS, not data engineering.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, Amazon EKS
authors: Balaji Mohan, Muthu Pitchaimani, Senthil Ramasamy
